items.title: CAKE kernel candidates for MiniMax-H3 on B300 and RTX 5090
items.author: yyihuang
items.body_excerpt:
# CAKE kernel candidates for MiniMax-H3 on B300 and RTX 5090

Thank you for inviting customized kernel challenges in the CAKE tracker. We have
a MiniMax-H3 FL2VA runtime based on Sol Engine and SGLang and would like to ask
whether any of the standalone kernels below would be useful CAKE challenges.

These are independent candidates rather than a request for the CAKE team to
implement all of them. We will take care of Sol Engine/SGLang integration,
collectives, quantized checkpoints, calibration, end-to-end validation, and
deployment.

The two targets are:

- NVIDIA B300 / SM103a, with Ulysses SP1/SP2/SP4/SP8;
- NVIDIA RTX 5090 / SM120, quantized execution and SP1 only.

## B300 / SM103a candidates

Common H3 dimensions:

- hidden size: 5,376
- heads: 56
- head dimension: 128
- attention inner dimension: 7,168
- FFN dimension: 14,336
- supported Ulysses degree `P`: 1, 2, 4, or 8
- heads per rank after all-to-all: `56 / P` = 56, 28, 14, or 7
- non-causal packed-varlen attention
- batch size: 1

For B300, we are interested in separate shape specializations for SP1, SP2,
SP4, and SP8.

Nominal `M` values for our main 768p duration buckets are:

| Duration | Global packed rows `T` | SP1 `M` | SP2 `M` | SP4 `M` | SP8 `M` |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 s | 33,472 | 33,472 | 16,736 | 8,368 | 4,184 |
| 5 s | 38,592 | 38,592 | 19,296 | 9,648 | 4,824 |
| 6 s | 48,768 | 48,768 | 24,384 | 12,192 | 6,096 |
| 8 s | 58,944 | 58,944 | 29,472 | 14,736 | 7,368 |
| 10 s | 74,240 | 74,240 | 37,120 | 18,560 | 9,280 |
| 15 s | 109,952 | 109,952 | 54,976 | 27,488 | 13,744 |

Prompt length makes `M` slightly dynamic, so kernels need tail handling around
these values. We can provide exact tensor traces and a PyTorch reference for each
operator below.

## 1. Fused BF16 pre-attention kernel — highest priority

Reference operation:

```text
x [M, 5376]
  -> RMSNorm
  -> indexed AdaLN scale/shift
  -> BF16 QKV GEMM [M, 5376] x [5376, 21504]
  -> Q/K RMSNorm over D=128
  -> 3-D RoPE on Q/K
  -> destination-major BF16 QKV
       [P, M, 56/P, 3, 128]
```

The output is only a send buffer; NCCL all-to-all is outside the kernel. The goal
is to avoid writing normalized x, modulated x, ordinary QKV, normalized Q/K, and
RoPE Q/K to HBM. `P` may be implemented as four compile-time specializations
instead of one dynamic kernel if that produces better code.

## 2. Fused low-precision pre-attention kernels

Same operation and output layout as kernel 1, with two independent variants:

```text
A. MXFP8/FP8 QKV GEMM
   -> BF16 Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE
   -> destination-major E4M3 QKV + scales

B. NVFP4 W4A4 QKV GEMM
   -> BF16 Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE
   -> destination-major NVFP4 QKV + block scales
```

An additional NVFP4-GEMM-to-E4M3-output variant is useful if the matching NVFP4
attention kernel is not accurate enough.

We will provide prepacked weights and scale tensors. The kernel does not need to
create or calibrate quantized weights.

### Candidate 2 implementation tracking

- [ ] https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5060 — Variant A: MXFP8 pre-attention for B200 (`sm_100a`) and B300 (`sm_103a`). Implementation and validation are complete; the PR is open for review.


## 3. Packed-varlen FlashAttention-4 kernels

Input after our existing Ulysses all-to-all:

```text
Q/K/V: [T, 56/P, 128]
cu_seqlens: int32
causal: false
output: BF16 [T, 56/P, 128]
```

Nominal `T` centers are 33,472, 38,592, 48,768, 58,944, 74,240, and
109,952. Requested standalone variants:

```text
A. BF16 FA4
B. E4M3 FP8 FA4 with explicit descales
C. experimental block-scaled NVFP4 FA4
```

For C, we would be interested in a genuine low-precision Tensor Core implementation
rather than NVFP4 storage followed by BF16 matmuls. Softmax remains FP32. It would
be helpful to report the actual QK and PV MMA dtypes separately; a hybrid
NVFP4-QK / FP8-or-BF16-PV candidate would also be useful.

## 4. Direct-layout attention output projection

Reference operation:

```text
inverse-Ulysses receive layout [P, M, 56/P, 128]
  -> read without a standalone unpack/transpose
  -> O GEMM [M, 7168] x [7168, 5376]
  -> indexed gate * output + residual
  -> BF16 [M, 5376]
```

Requested GEMM variants: BF16, MXFP8/FP8, and NVFP4 W4A4. The collective itself
is outside the kernel.

## 5. Fused RMSNorm + AdaLN + FC1 + SwiGLU

Reference operation:

```text
x [M, 5376]
  -> RMSNorm
  -> indexed AdaLN scale/shift
  -> FC1 [M, 5376] x [5376, 28672]
  -> split gate/up
  -> SiLU(gate) * up
  -> BF16 [M, 14336]
```

Requested GEMM variants: BF16, MXFP8/FP8, and NVFP4 W4A4.

## 6. Persistent full MLP candidate

Reference operation:

```text
RMSNorm + indexed AdaLN
  -> FC1 [M, 5376] x [5376, 28672]
  -> SwiGLU
  -> FC2 [M, 14336] x [14336, 5376]
  -> indexed gate * output + residual
  -> BF16 [M, 5376]
```

Requested variants: BF16, MXFP8/FP8, and NVFP4 W4A4. This is only worth keeping
if it beats kernel 5 plus a tuned standalone FC2 GEMM; CAKE does not need to solve
that scheduling decision outside the kernel benchmark.

## 7. Quantize-and-pack helper kernels

These are useful fallbacks when the GEMM epilogue cannot write the communication
layout directly:

```text
BF16 Q/K/V [M, 56, 128]
  -> destination-major E4M3 + scales [P, M, 56/P, 3, 128]

BF16 Q/K/V [M, 56, 128]
  -> destination-major NVFP4 + block scales [P, M, 56/P, 3, 128]
```

Quantization and relayout should happen in one HBM pass.

## RTX 5090 / SM120 quantized SP1 candidates

If CAKE currently supports SM120, we would also appreciate considering a smaller
set of single-GPU kernels for the quantized H3 FL2VA path on RTX 5090. This target
uses SP1 only, so there is no Ulysses layout or collective in these kernels.

For SP1, `M = T`; the nominal M values are 33,472, 38,592, 48,768, 58,944,
74,240, and 109,952 for 4/5/6/8/10/15 seconds. We are interested in two quantized
GEMM formats:

- W8A8 E4M3 FP8;
- NVIDIA-compatible block-scaled NVFP4 W4A4.

BF16 is used as the numerical reference but does not need a separately tu

items.title: KV cache token validation rejects every L2 block that has a prefix: unpack_tokens() decodes the wrong bytes
items.author: wguo7
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

With `AIBRIX_KV_CACHE_OL_TOKEN_VALIDATION_ENABLED=1`, `L2Cache.get()` checks the tokens stored in each fetched block against the requested key, using `ManagedMemoryRegion.unpack_tokens()` (`aibrix_kvcache/memory/allocator.py`). `pack_tokens()` writes `[cache block, magic, footer (prefix_length, query_length), prefix + query tokens]`. When an MR has no tokens cached on the object, `unpack_tokens()` decodes them from its buffer, and that decoding is wrong. This is the case on every L2 get: `KVCacheManager` allocates fresh MRs with `allocate_for()` ([cache_manager.py#L1321](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/8e967422b320de5e1ade879ce8fcd42ab1632735/python/aibrix_kvcache/aibrix_kvcache/cache_manager.py#L1321)), each sized for its block's prefix + query tokens ([#L1497-L1503](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/8e967422b320de5e1ade879ce8fcd42ab1632735/python/aibrix_kvcache/aibrix_kvcache/cache_manager.py#L1497-L1503)), and passes them to `self._l2_cache.get()` ([#L1333](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/8e967422b320de5e1ade879ce8fcd42ab1632735/python/aibrix_kvcache/aibrix_kvcache/cache_manager.py#L1333)), which fills them from the backend and then calls `unpack_tokens()`. The decoding goes wrong in two ways:

- The prefix is read from the footer slice, so it decodes as `[prefix_length, query_length]`.
- The query is read as the first `query_length` tokens after the footer, which are the start of the prefix.

As a result, `_tokens_match()` fails for every block whose key has a prefix, that is, every block after the first one of a sequence, and `L2Cache.get()` counts it as a miss. Only the first block of each sequence can hit in L2, so the rest have to be computed again. Token validation is off by default, so this affects deployments that turn it on. The existing round-trip tests do not catch this because they unpack the same MR they packed, and `unpack_tokens()` then returns the tokens cached on the object.

### Steps to Reproduce

The script packs a block with a 16-token prefix and 16-token query, copies its bytes into a fresh MR and unpacks it (part 1). It then puts two blocks of one sequence through `L2Cache` with the `MOCK` backend and gets them back (part 2). Output on main (8e96742):

```
[1] actual: prefix=[16, 16] query[:4]=[100, 101, 102, 103]
[1] expected: prefix=[100, 101, 102, 103]... (len 16) query[:4]=[116, 117, 118, 119]
[2] put status: Status(error_code=StatusCodes.OK, value=2)
[2] actual: L2Cache.get() of 2 stored blocks -> Status(error_code=StatusCodes.OK, value=1)
[2] expected: OK with value 2
```

<details><summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
"""unpack_tokens() decodes prefix and query wrongly for an MR filled from bytes.

Run: KVCACHE_SRC=<aibrix>/python/aibrix_kvcache python -u repro.py
"""

import os
import sys
import warnings
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
os.environ["AIBRIX_KV_CACHE_OL_TOKEN_VALIDATION_ENABLED"] = "1"
sys.path.insert(0, os.environ.get("KVCACHE_SRC", "."))

import asyncio  # noqa: E402

import torch  # noqa: E402

from aibrix_kvcache import TokenListView  # noqa: E402
from aibrix_kvcache.l2 import L2Cache  # noqa: E402
from aibrix_kvcache.l2.key_builders import KeyBuilder  # noqa: E402
from aibrix_kvcache.memory import ManagedMemoryRegion, MemoryRegion, TensorPoolAllocator  # noqa: E402
from aibrix_kvcache.spec import (  # noqa: E402
    KVCacheBlockLayout,
    KVCacheBlockSpec,
    KVCacheTensorSpec,
)

assert not MemoryRegion.use_compact_layout()
BLK = 16
BLOCK_NBYTES = 64

# ---- Part 1: pure MR round trip through bytes ---------------------------
alloc = TensorPoolAllocator.create(capacity_nbytes=1 << 20)
all_tokens = TokenListView(list(range(100, 100 + 2 * BLK)))
prefix, query = all_tokens[:BLK], all_tokens[BLK:]
size = ManagedMemoryRegion.calculate_size(BLOCK_NBYTES, 2 * BLK)

src = alloc.alloc(size).get()[0]
src.block_nbytes = BLOCK_NBYTES
src.pack_tokens(prefix=prefix, query=query)
src.seal()

dst = alloc.alloc(size).get()[0]  # fresh MR, as handed to a backend get()
dst.block_nbytes = BLOCK_NBYTES
dst.slab[dst.addr : dst.addr + src.length].copy_(
    src.slab[src.addr : src.addr + src.length]
)
p, q = dst.unpack_tokens()
print(f"[1] actual: prefix={list(p.to_numpy())} query[:4]={list(q.to_numpy()[:4])}")
print(f"[1] expected: prefix={list(prefix.to_numpy()[:4])}... (len {BLK}) "
      f"query[:4]={list(query.to_numpy()[:4])}")

# ---- Part 2: end to end through L2Cache with the MOCK backend ------------
spec = KVCacheBlockSpec(
    block_ntokens=BLK,
    block_dtype=torch.float16,
    block_layout=KVCacheBlockLayout.NCLD,
    tensor_spec=KVCacheTensorSpec(heads=[0], layers=[0], head_size=1),
)
l2 = L2Cache(
    backend_name="MOCK",
    placement_policy="SIMPLE",
    namespace="t",
    block_spec=spec,
    executor=ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2),
    key_builder=KeyBuilder.create("ROLLING_HASH", block_size=BLK),
)
assert l2.open().is_ok()


def mk(prefix_v, query_v, pack):
    n = (len(prefix_v) if prefix_v is not None else 0) + len(query_v)
    mr = alloc.alloc(ManagedMemoryRegion.calculate_size(spec.block_nbytes, n)).get()[0]
    mr.block_nbytes = spec.block_nbytes
    if pack:
        mr.pack_tokens(prefix=prefix_v, query=query_v)
        mr.seal()
    return mr


async def main():
    put_mrs = [mk(None, prefix, True), mk(prefix, query, True)]
    st = await l2.put(None, all_tokens, put_mrs)
    print(f"[2] put status: {st}")
    get_mrs = [mk(None, prefix, False), mk(prefix, query, False)]
    st = await l2.get(None, all_tokens, get_mrs)
    return st


st = asyncio.run(main())
print(f"[2] actual: L2Cache.get() of 2 stored blocks -> {st}")
print("[2] expected: OK with value 2")
os._exit(0)
```

</details>

### Expected behavior

`unpack_tokens()` returns the packed prefix and query, and `L2Cache.get()` of the two stored blocks returns 2.

### Environment

- AIBrix version: main at 8e96742
- Deployment environment: none. The repro uses

items.title: [QST] SM120 FP8 MMA with FP32 accumulate, plain form against block-scaled form with unit scales
items.author: emre570
items.body_excerpt:
**What is your question?**

On an RTX 5080, the plain FP8 MMA with FP32 accumulate runs at half the rate of the block-scaled FP8 MMA with FP32 accumulate. When all scale bytes are `0x7F` (UE8M0 1.0), the two forms give equal bits.

My FP8 attention kernel in CuTe DSL used `MmaFP8Op`. I changed it to `MmaMXF8Op` with constant unit scales and no other change. The kernel time went from 123.6 ms to 83.6 ms and the output is byte-equal (sgl-project/sglang#43390). So a user can do this today. My question is about the default.

1. Is there a reason to keep the plain form for E4M3 x E4M3 with FP32 accumulate on SM120?
2. If there is no reason, do you want `MmaFP8Op` and `rr_op_selector_sm120` to emit the block-scaled form with unit scales for this case? I can send a PR.

### Related report

The same behavior is reported in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5963 for the FlashInfer SM120 FP8 attention kernel, with RTX 5090 numbers and a bit-identity check. That issue also points to the MXFP8 attention work in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3628 and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4149. The numbers below add an RTX 5080 and a CUTLASS GEMM measurement to that report.

### Scope

E4M3 x E4M3, FP32 accumulate, one RTX 5080 (driver 595.99.02, CUDA 13.3, CUTLASS `ffa119a12`). I did not measure other types or other cards.

### Raw MMA rate

Independent MMA chains, no memory access, 84 SMs. The rate is the same from 4 to 32 warps per SM.

| instruction | TFLOP/s |
|---|---:|
| `kind::f8f6f4.m16n8k32 ... f32.e4m3.e4m3.f32` | 246 |
| `kind::mxf8f6f4.block_scale.scale_vec::1X.m16n8k32 ... f32.e4m3.e4m3.f32.ue8m0` | 489 |

### Bit equality

- Random finite inputs. 0 of 704,643,072 accumulator registers differ.
- Negative control with scale 2.0. 704,643,071 registers differ.
- Edge cases (subnormal, ±448, NaN bytes, accumulator start at zero, FLT_MAX, subnormal, infinity, NaN). 30 classes, 176,160,768 registers each, 0 bits differ.

### CUTLASS GEMM

I used the SM120 `CollectiveBuilder` with `OpClassTensorOp`, pingpong schedule, tile 128x128x128, FP32 output. Then I changed only the instruction in `SM120_16x8x32_TN<float_e4m3_t, float_e4m3_t, float>` to the block-scaled form. The scale `0x7F7F7F7F` stays in a register. There is no scale factor tensor and no additional load. The patch is 34 lines.

I measured 30 shapes from real models. All 30 give 0 different output words. Five examples:

| shape source | M x N x K | plain | patched | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Wan 2.2 14B, `to_q` | 32760 x 5120 x 5120 | 236.1 | 398.6 | 1.69x |
| Llama 3.3 70B, MLP up | 4096 x 28672 x 8192 | 234.7 | 398.1 | 1.70x |
| FLUX.1-dev, FFN up | 4608 x 12288 x 3072 | 231.8 | 393.3 | 1.70x |
| MiniMax-H3, FFN up | 30272 x 14336 x 5376 | 234.6 | 363.5 | 1.55x |
| Gemma 3 27B, MLP up | 128 x 21504 x 5376 | 195.8 | 203.4 | 1.04x |

TFLOP/s. The speedup is 1.55x to 1.72x for the 22 shapes with M of 4096 or more. It is 1.04x to 1.82x for the 8 shapes with M = 128, where the low end is DRAM-bound.

Nsight Compute on the stock plain kernel shows the tensor pipe 96% busy. The MMA instruction rate is 47.9% of the peak.

One caution. These numbers use `max_swizzle_size = 8`. With the default of 1, three large shapes become DRAM-bound and the patched kernel is slower than the plain kernel (0.88x). I can open a different issue for that with the data.

### Where the plain form is used

- CuTe DSL `MmaFP8Op`
- `rr_op_selector_sm120` in `sm120_mma_builder.inl`, `sm120_array_mma_builder.inl` and `sm120_blockwise_mma_builder.inl`

cuBLASLt on the same card uses `QMMA.SF.16832.F32.E4M3.E4M3.E8` in its FP8 GEMM kernel and no plain `QMMA`.

I can share the benchmark source, the patch and the raw results if they are useful.

items.title: Expert Parallelism (EP) roadmap for SM12x b12x MoE kernel (b12x_fused_moe / B12xMoEWrapper)
items.author: ItamarTerem
items.body_excerpt:
Hi flashinfer team,
We're deploying a large MoE model (384 experts, top_k=8) on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120/Blackwell workstation) using the b12x_fused_moe CuteDSL kernel via TensorRT-LLM's pytorch backend, and have hit the Expert Parallelism restriction:

b12x_fused_moe does not yet support Expert Parallelism
(num_local_experts={X} != num_experts={Y}).
Use a different MoE backend for EP configurations.

This comes from the explicit guard in flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/b12x_moe.py (both in the free function b12x_fused_moe and in B12xMoEWrapper.__init__), confirmed in flashinfer version 0.6.12.
Context on why this matters for us specifically: without EP, every GPU must retain workspace/routing capacity sized for the full state_E (all 384 experts), even though tensor parallelism already shards each expert's weights across GPUs. This is a meaningful, measured memory cost — in our case, the dynamic workspace's packed_input buffer alone accounts for roughly 7–11GB/GPU across a 60-MoE-layer model, purely from having to size for the worst-case "all experts active" scenario rather than a num_experts/ep_size subset.

What we're asking:

1. Is EP support for the SM12x b12x kernel family (static/dynamic/micro backends) on the roadmap, even at a preliminary stage?
2. Is there a rough timeline or tracking issue we could follow?
3. Are there known architectural blockers specific to SM120 (vs. SM100/SM103, where other kernels like MegaMoE already support EP) that make this a harder problem here?

We also note that vLLM's FlashInferB12xExperts (_supports_parallel_config) explicitly declines to use this backend when EP is requested, for the same underlying reason — so this appears to be a shared, cross-framework limitation rather than something specific to our integration.
Happy to provide more detail on our exact shapes/config if useful. Thanks for your work on this — the b12x kernel has otherwise been the only correctness-verified MoE path we've found for SM120 (CUTLASS produces silently incorrect output on this architecture in our testing).

In the VM deployment guide, note that existing `ray up` clusters update their worker nodes once after upgrading to a Ray version with the auth token file mount (#67050): each worker reruns its setup commands and restarts Ray, and in Docker mode its container restarts. Instances aren't relaunched.

Also say in the docs and the release notes that an auth rejection now raises `AuthenticationError` at once, where `ray.init(address=...)` used to raise `ConnectionError` after retrying. `AuthenticationError` subclasses `ConnectionError`, so existing handlers still catch it.

Also document that `ray start --head` needs a token created first with `ray get-auth-token --generate`, and that the token must then be copied to every node.

Must land in the same release as #67055.

items.title: [Bug] Batch templates emit arguments rejected by SGLang 0.5.22 and vLLM 0.32.0
items.author: Jackmeson1
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

Accepted optional batch settings produce incompatible arguments:

- **SGLang 0.5.22 translation:** `parallelism.pp=2` emits ambiguous `--pp 2`; `engine_args.block_size=16` emits unrecognized `--block-size 16`.
- **vLLM 0.32.0 compatibility:** `engine_args.swap_space=4` emits unrecognized `--swap-space 4`. `quantization.weight=bf16` emits `--quantization bf16`: argparse accepts it, but quantization validation rejects it as an unknown method.

Both baseline argument lists parse. SGLang forwards unmapped typed fields; vLLM emits flags independently of engine.version (`python/aibrix/aibrix/batch/manifest/engine_adapter.py:128,156,228,241`).

Report only; we are not working on a fix.

### Steps to Reproduce

At the AIBrix commit below, with its Python dependencies installed, save as `repro.py` at repository root:

```python
import argparse
import contextlib
import io
import json
import sys
from types import SimpleNamespace as NS

mode = sys.argv[1]
if mode == "render":
    from aibrix.batch.manifest.engine_adapter import build_engine_args
    from aibrix.batch.template import ModelDeploymentTemplateSpec as Spec

    rows = []
    for engine, version, changes in [
        ("sglang", "0.5.22", [{}, {"parallelism": {"pp": 2}},
                            {"engine_args": {"block_size": 16}}]),
        ("vllm", "0.32.0", [{}, {"engine_args": {"swap_space": 4}},
                          {"quantization": {"weight": "bf16"}}]),
    ]:
        for change in changes:
            spec = Spec.model_validate(dict(
                engine=dict(type=engine, version=version, image=engine),
                model_source=dict(type="huggingface", uri="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B"),
                accelerator=dict(type="H100", count=change.get("parallelism", {}).get("pp", 1)),
                supported_endpoints=["/v1/chat/completions"], **change))
            rows.append([engine, build_engine_args(spec)])
    print(json.dumps(rows))
else:
    if mode == "sglang":
        from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=mode)
        ServerArgs.add_cli_args(parser)
    else:
        from vllm.entrypoints.launchers.cli_args import make_arg_parser
        from vllm.utils.argparse_utils import FlexibleArgumentParser
        from vllm.config.model import ModelConfig
        parser = make_arg_parser(FlexibleArgumentParser(prog=mode))
    for engine, argv in json.load(open("cases.json")):
        if engine != mode:
            continue
        print("argv:", *argv)
        errors = io.StringIO()
        try:
            with contextlib.redirect_stderr(errors):
                parsed = parser.parse_args(argv)
        except SystemExit:
            print(errors.getvalue().splitlines()[-1])
            continue
        print("argparse: ACCEPT")
        if mode == "vllm":
            try:
                ModelConfig._verify_quantization(NS(
                    quantization=parsed.quantization,
                    model_arch_config=NS(quantization_config=None),
                    allow_deprecated_quantization=False))
            except ValueError as error:
                print("later validation:", error)
```

Render:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=python/aibrix python repro.py render > cases.json
```

Replay from the same directory in separate Python 3.12 environments:

```sh
# SGLang environment
pip install sglang==0.5.22
python repro.py sglang
# vLLM environment
pip install vllm==0.32.0
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python repro.py vllm
```

### Expected behavior

Accepted template settings produce arguments compatible with the selected engine/version.

### Environment

AIBrix `b389a59a58ea`; Linux CPU; Python 3.10 rendering/3.12 parsers; engine sources verified against tags v0.5.22/v0.32.0. Validation calls the real quantization validator without model initialization. No server launched. The sample pins vLLM 0.6.3; its launch behavior was not tested.

### Area

Batch

items.title: [Feature] Add DeepInfer as a supported inference engine
items.author: googs1025
items.body_excerpt:
### 🚀 Feature Description and Motivation

[DeepInfer](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer) is DeepSeek's newly open-sourced high-performance inference framework for large-scale DeepSeek model inference.

AIBrix currently supports multiple inference engines, including vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, and xLLM. This issue proposes adding DeepInfer as another supported engine.

The integration would allow users to deploy and operate DeepInfer workloads through AIBrix and use AIBrix for Kubernetes orchestration, request routing, autoscaling, observability, and, where the engine contracts permit, KV-cache and disaggregated inference management.

DeepInfer currently provides offline inference and explicitly lists several components required for a complete online inference service as not yet included:

- KV-cache system
- VE/Prefill/Decode disaggregation
- Load balancing across data-parallel prefill and decode replicas

Because an online serving API and metrics contract are not yet available, the integration should be developed incrementally as those interfaces become stable.

### Use Case

Users serving DeepSeek models on NVIDIA SM100 GPUs or Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs may want to use DeepInfer's optimized kernels, scheduling, parallelism, and deterministic inference capabilities while relying on AIBrix for the Kubernetes control plane.

A target deployment should eventually support:

- Declaring `model.aibrix.ai/engine: deepinfer`
- Deploying DeepInfer workers using Deployment or StormService
- Routing inference requests through AIBrix Gateway
- Discovering ready DeepInfer replicas
- Mapping DeepInfer metrics to AIBrix's engine-neutral metrics
- Applying supported routing and autoscaling policies
- Providing a documented example for a DeepInfer-supported DeepSeek model

### Proposed Solution

Implement the integration in stages.

#### Phase 1: Define the serving contract

Coordinate with the DeepInfer project and document the interfaces required by AIBrix:

- Online inference API and streaming behavior
- Model-name and error-response semantics
- Health and readiness endpoints
- Prometheus metrics endpoint and metric names
- Container image and startup configuration
- Prefill/decode role and transfer metadata, when available

The initial integration should not assume that DeepInfer is OpenAI-compatible until that contract is provided and verified.

#### Phase 2: Basic AIBrix engine support

Once DeepInfer provides an online serving interface:

- Add `deepinfer` as a supported value of `model.aibrix.ai/engine`
- Add the available metric mappings
- Support pod discovery, health checking, and ordinary gateway routing
- Add a sample deployment for supported hardware and models
- Add integration tests covering request forwarding and failure propagation
- Document supported and unsupported AIBrix routing policies

Gateway-tracked routing policies may be enabled before engine-metric-based policies when the required metrics are unavailable.

#### Phase 3: Advanced integration

Track advanced capabilities separately as their DeepInfer contracts stabilize:

- KV-cache-aware routing
- VE/Prefill/Decode disaggregation
- Independent scaling of data-parallel prefill and decode replicas
- DeepInfer-specific runtime management
- NVIDIA and Ascend deployment validation

### Initial Completion Criteria

- [ ] A stable DeepInfer online serving contract is documented
- [ ] `model.aibrix.ai/engine: deepinfer` is recognized
- [ ] AIBrix Gateway can route requests to DeepInfer replicas
- [ ] Health/readiness and supported metrics are integrated
- [ ] At least one reproducible deployment sample is provided
- [ ] Integration and error-path tests are included
- [ ] Documentation clearly lists supported hardware, models, APIs, metrics, routing policies, and known limitations

### Area

Runtime

items.title: [Performance]: Kimi K3 decode runs the MoE-tail additions as separate kernels before the next attention-residual
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### Proposal to improve performance

In Kimi K3 decode, every MoE layer ends with `prefix_sum + (routed_out + shared_out)` (`KimiK3MoERuntime.forward` returns `routed_out + shared_out`, then `KimiLinearDecoderLayer.forward` adds it to the prefix sum). These are two small elementwise kernels per MoE layer. Their result is read first by the next layer's pre-attention attention-residual + RMSNorm, or by the model's output attention-residual + norm. In the decode window, that consumer is already `trtllm::attn_res_add_rmsnorm_fwd`'s kernel family, which loads the prefix sum as its last candidate and can already fold one addend into it.

Proposal: give `trtllm::attn_res_add_rmsnorm_fwd` an optional second addend (`layer_residual_add2`) that computes `bf16(prefix + bf16(routed + shared))`, rounding exactly like the two BF16 tensor additions. Then add an opt-in path in which a MoE layer hands `(prefix, routed, shared)` to that consumer instead of adding them itself. Wherever the consumer would not take the fused per-token kernel (a hidden-state capture layer for speculative decoding, no snapshots yet, the persistent kernel, shapes outside the fused window), the addition is done first and the existing code runs unchanged.

Measured on Rubin, TP8 across 2 nodes (MNNVL), Kimi K3 with speculative decoding, CUDA graphs, single request, decode step time, same change on our integration branch: -0.106 / -0.117 / -0.121 / -0.126 / -0.107 / -0.107 ms at 2K / 32K / 64K / 96K / 128K / 393K context. Accuracy and needle checks unchanged; the materialized prefix sums are bitwise identical.

PR to follow (draft, opt-in via an environment variable).

items.title: [Feature][Rubin] CAKE four-stream mHC training at H4096 with FP32 mapping and full backward
items.author: abcdabcd987
items.body_excerpt:
## Problem

We need efficient four-stream mHC training, including normalization, mapping, collapse, residual mixing, and all activation/parameter gradients. Existing [MegaMHC exports](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/e403d30785ea9ece65a88b3337db86dcac19fef5/flashinfer/experimental/deepgemm_mega_mhc/mega_mhc.py) target H5120 with FP8-output machinery and do not expose this complete BF16-activation training backward.

In a two-update GB200 profile, mHC-only work consumes 3.151 s, or 5.39% of 58.432 s summed GPU kernel duration. This excludes the attention/MLP branch and its checkpoint replay; it is not an end-to-end speedup estimate.

The main targets are FP32 mapping GEMMs (1.537 s) and normalization/combined input-gradient work (0.987 s), rather than coefficients/Sinkhorn alone (0.039 s). A materialized normalized FP32 `[T,16384]` tensor is 0.91–0.99 GiB at the profiled token counts; this is per-tensor size, not a measured simultaneous memory peak.

## Requested outcome

Support the complete four-stream mHC connection at hidden size 4096, with runtime-variable local token counts, BF16 activation boundaries, FP32 mapping/coefficient arithmetic and gradients, and first-order backward through all mHC paths. The attention/MLP branch remains an external operation; split prepare/finish kernels are fine if the complete gradient accumulation contract is preserved.

Prioritize eliminating large intermediates or fusing normalization with mapping/gradient work. Do not limit the request to a forward Sinkhorn optimization.

## Target hardware

- SM100 (B200, GB200): profiled target.
- SM103 (B300, GB300): requested target.
- Future architecture: SM107 / Rubin, requested training support.

## Inference engine

PyTorch native; Custom / other. Training with activation checkpointing.

## Affected model or model family

[GLM-5.3-Flash, pinned public configuration](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash/blob/eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a/config.json), with four streams, hidden size 4096, 20 Sinkhorn iterations, and `hc_eps=1e-6`. The requested FP32 intermediate policy below is explicit; bitwise equivalence to a model implementation that rounds intermediate coefficients to BF16 is not the target.

## Workload and configuration

- **Local tokens:** observed `T ∈ {14928,15288,15566,15590,16114,16132,16164,16263}`; these are benchmark points, not an allowed-value list or a 16K maximum. Support runtime-variable `T`, including smaller/larger and irregular local shards.
- **Parallelism:** motivating run uses world size 64, CP16 and EP32; this request is for local mHC kernels, not collectives. Different CP sizes and batch layouts change local `T`; no CP16-specific geometry is required.
- **Model-fixed dimensions:** four residual streams, hidden size 4096, and the resulting 24-by-16384 mapping are not divided by CP in this path. Keep those model dimensions as the required scope rather than incorrectly replacing four streams with `4 / CP`.
- **Quantization:** none in the requested mHC path; no FP8 output requirement.
- **Environment:** `python -m flashinfer.collect_env` output is unavailable.

| Operand | Shape | Dtype | Element strides / role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Streams `X` | `[T,4,4096]` | BF16 | Contiguous `[16384,4096,1]` |
| Mapping `fn` | `[24,16384]` | FP32 | Row-major `[16384,1]`; use its transpose for forward |
| `scale`, `base` | `[3]`, `[24]` | FP32 | Contiguous |
| Collapsed input `U`, branch output `B` | `[T,4096]` | BF16 | Contiguous |
| Mixed output `Y`, upstream `dY` | `[T,4,4096]` | BF16 | Same logical layout as streams |
| `dfn`, `dscale`, `dbase` | Same shapes as parameters | FP32 | FP32 reductions and returned gradients |

### Exact function

Use `rms_eps=1e-5`, `hc_eps=1e-6`, and 20 finite Sinkhorn iterations. The following pseudocode defines the requested function, with arithmetic in FP32 except the marked activation boundaries:

```text
u = float32(X).reshape(T, 16384)
r = rsqrt(mean(u*u, axis=-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-5)
z = (u*r) @ fn.T
pre  = sigmoid(z[:, :4]  * scale[0] + base[:4]) + 1e-6
post = 2 * sigmoid(z[:, 4:8] * scale[1] + base[4:8])
logits = (z[:, 8:] * scale[2] + base[8:]).reshape(T,4,4)
C = row_softmax(logits) + 1e-6
C = C / (column_sum(C) + 1e-6)
repeat 19 times:
    C = C / (row_sum(C) + 1e-6)
    C = C / (column_sum(C) + 1e-6)
U[t,d] = BF16(sum_i pre[t,i] * float32(X[t,i,d]))
B = external_branch(U)  # BF16 [T,4096]
Y[t,j,d] = BF16(post[t,j] * float32(B[t,d])
                 + sum_i C[t,i,j] * float32(X[t,i,d]))
```

`C` is indexed by source stream then destination stream. Different normalization order, epsilon placement, or differentiating an idealized converged Sinkhorn solution would change the function.

### Backward precision

Mapping GEMMs must preserve FP32-quality arithmetic; BF16/TF32 approximations should be explicit, separately validated modes rather than silent replacements. Keep mapping intermediates, coefficients, their gradients, and parameter reductions in FP32.

Return the branch-output gradient in BF16 after its complete FP32 sum. After branch backward supplies `dU`, sum the mapping, collapse, and residual-mix contributions to `dX` in FP32, then cast once to BF16. Returning three separately rounded BF16 contributions is not equivalent. Preserve sigmoid-tail gradients even when the FP32 forward sigmoid rounds to one.

## Current workaround

Custom normalization/coefficient/stream kernels plus FP32 library GEMMs and a combined autograd boundary. The implementation supports training, but mapping and large-intermediate traffic are costly; a forward-only FP8-oriented route is not a replacement.

## Impact

Throughput; Memory capacity or bandwidth; Correctness or numerical-quality risk.

## Acceptance criteria

- Validate `Y`, `dX`, `dB`, `dfn`, `dscale`, and `dbase` against independent eager references that implement the finite normalization chain and stated storage boundaries.
- Cover single-cast cancellation cases, satur

items.title: [cake deslop] deepgemm fp8/fp4/kgroup/mixed/batched GEMMs (2): share 215 TMA encoders, drop exact-shape programs, template clones
items.author: yyihuang
items.body_excerpt:
**Background.** This issue covers the five Cake-generated DeepGEMM-signature GEMM families: `csrc/experimental/deepgemm_{fp8,fp4,kgroup,mixed,batched}_gemm` plus `flashinfer/experimental/deepgemm_*`. They are reached through the `@flashinfer_experimental_api` wrappers `flashinfer/{fp8_batched_gemm,fp4_gemm,fp4_k_grouped_gemm,fp8_fp4_gemm}.py` and through `prepare_fp8_gemm_1d1d`, and they run on sm_100a/sm_103a only. They are JIT-only via `gen_jit_spec`; none appear in `flashinfer/aot.py`. At 3184bbea the unit is 124 files / 47,246 lines: 43 kernel `.cu` (24,170), 43 binding `.cu` (16,279), 16 Python files (4,215) and 8 test files (1,797). Per family, kernel/binding lines are fp8 1,128/728 (2 programs), fp4 3,250/2,792 (8), kgroup 12,845/7,568 (19), mixed 3,138/2,944 (8) and batched 3,809/2,247 (6). Nothing in `tests/gemm` references these families. Round 1 regenerated every family on 2026-10-02/03, folding in perf PRs #5739 and #5754:
- #5831 → #5912 (fp8): 4 raw-PTX single-shape programs → 2 runtime-shape sources.
- #5830 → #5935 (fp4): 20 → 8.
- #5832 → #5925 (kgroup): 48 + JSON → 19.
- #5835 → #5941 (mixed): 24 → 8.
- #5828 → #5931 (batched): 24 → 6.
- #5813 → #5928 added the shared `flashinfer/experimental/deepgemm_common` loader. None of these families adopted it; only mega_moe_v3 did, in #6034.

No commit has touched these paths since, so nothing was re-added. What remains is generated host duplication plus the exact-shape programs that round 1 kept on purpose. All 43 programs are referenced by a route table, so there are no never-compiled sources.

**Findings**
- **Generated TMA encoders and smem helper (host only).** The 43 bindings define 215 `inline CUtensorMap EncodeTma_*` functions, 9,044 lines or 55% of the binding text (fp8 10/396, fp4 40/1,596, kgroup 95/4,168, mixed 40/1,594, batched 30/1,290). Each is the same ~42-line `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` wrapper, specialised on dtype, rank, box, swizzle and L2 promotion. 27 bindings (fp8 2, kgroup 19, batched 6) inline a 19-line `CakeSetMaxDynamicSmem` (513 lines). The 16 fp4/mixed bindings include `cake_deepgemm_{fp4,mixed}_gemm_host_common.cuh` (56/55 lines) instead; those headers already contain the helper and differ from each other by one SPDX line. `csrc/tvm_ffi_utils.h` has neither helper. This contradicts #5928's "carry no inlined helper block".
- **Dead host code and duplicate artifacts.**
  - In `deepgemm_fp8_gemm/cake_jit.py`, `supported_arches()` (lines 105-111) has 0 callers, and `runtime.py` never reads the two `closure_sha256` dicts (60-63, 90-93).
  - The flat-table branch of `route_table` in `kgroup_gemm.py` (717-730) can never collect anything, because `ROUTES` is always keyed by arch.
  - `csrc/experimental/deepgemm_kgroup_gemm/generated/.clang-format` is identical to `csrc/experimental/.clang-format`. #5928 said #5925 would delete it.
  - The unit has 5 byte-identical 21-line `DEEPGEMM_NOTICE.txt` files.
- **Ignored knobs.**
  - `descriptor_workspace` is accepted and then deleted (`flashinfer/fp4_gemm.py:23`, `fp4_gemm.py:842`, `batched_gemm.py:411-416`).
  - fp8 `runtime.py:173` deletes `cache_dir`.
  - `use_psum_layout` is only stored in `GroupedFP4Plan.options`, and "psum" appears in no generated kgroup source.
  - `block_n`/`epilogue_store_n` must be 128/32, and kgroup `num_stages` must be 7.
  - The fp8 sources sit one directory deeper (`deepgemm_fp8_gemm/cake_deepgemm_fp8_gemm/`) than every other family's.
- **kgroup exact-shape routes (6 of 19 programs).**
  - `small_2x8x3:{bf16,fp32,fp32_acc}` (`bac08f`/`4af7ea`/`731a5a`, 3,151 lines including ~93 registry lines). `route_candidates` (`kgroup_gemm.py:691-697`, `_SMALL_EXACT_GEOMETRIES={(2,8,3)}`) appends it only for m≤256, n==128, exactly 3 groups and max padded K>768. The runtime `small` tier always comes next, at the same grid. In a 9,504-point (m,n,k) sweep it is selected at 32 points on sm_100a (16 per SM count) and 16 on sm_103a.
  - Its kernel differs from `small` by 15 hunks / 103 lines. Every difference is a tile-scheduler constant that `small` instead reads from six host fast-division slots. The bindings are identical after normalisation.
  - #5925 kept this trio as a perf floor for the test-only 256x128 [2049,0,511] rows, where the runtime program measured 0.968/0.987/0.981 of the exact programs on ~5-us rows. The "correctness-only rows?" question on #5832 has had no answer since 2026-10-02.
  - `swapped:{fp32 | bf16, fp32_acc}` (`72e983` | `26c5ac`, `a6fc1f`; 3,275 lines). `schedule_tier` (:650-656) selects it only for (m,n)==(5120,2304) on 148/152-SM parts. `n256` is always the next candidate, and GB200 bf16 already runs `n256:bf16` at this shape. #5832 compared it to the old per-shape programs (0.993-1.002), but never to `n256`.
- **batched exact-shape and geometry-baked routes.**
  - `route_config` (`batched_gemm.py:305-308`) selects `bf16_t4`/`bf16_t128` (`df7ac6`/`c1767e`, 1,997 lines including ~54 registry lines) only for T ∈ {4,128}, (H,K,N)=(8,4096,1024) and `num_sms` in `PINNED_NUM_SMS=(148,152)`. That is 2 of 3,081 (T, SMs, epilogue) points for each program.
  - Plain bf16 at any other T raises `NotImplementedError`. With `alpha=1.0`, every T routes to `general_bm128_bn128_s5_alpha` (`ed2c9a`), which bakes in the same geometry.

items.title: autotune: a failed `trtllm_utils` JIT build is retried for every tactic and reported only as "unsupported tactic"
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

With flashinfer-python 0.6.18, 0.7.1, 0.7.2 and current main (5209e883), if the JIT module `trtllm_utils` (used by the
autotuner's `delay_kernel` before timing each tactic) cannot be built, `AutoTuner.choose_one` silently fails **every** tactic of
**every** profile:

- `get_trtllm_utils_module()` is wrapped in `functools.cache`, which does not cache exceptions, and `JitSpec.build()` runs
  ninja again on every call, so the build is started again for each tactic (~0.08 s per attempt in the single-process repro
  below, ~0.6 s per attempt with 4 ranks building concurrently in our server);
- `choose_one` catches the error per tactic and logs it at DEBUG level ("Skipping tactic ... due to failure while profiling:
  Ninja build failed"); the only INFO lines are "Skipped 32 unsupported tactic(s) for mxfp8_gemm" and, since 0.7, a single
  "Building JIT module trtllm_utils; this can take several minutes on first use." (`info_once`, so it reads as if one
  build were in progress);
- nothing reaches `profiling_cache`, so `autotune(cache=...)` writes no file and the op silently runs its fallback tactic.

In our deployment (one 4-GPU server, `mm_mxfp8` tuned through `autotune(True)` during warmup) this cost about 20 minutes of
startup per server (21 profiles x 32 tactics, repeated in several warmup passes) without producing any tuning result, and it took
debug logging to see that the cause was a build failure and not unsupported kernels.

On SM107 a JIT build of `trtllm_utils` happens even with `flashinfer-jit-cache-sm107a` installed: `aot.py` on main registers
`gen_trtllm_utils_module()` only for SM90 / SM100 / SM103 (#6795, open, adds SM107).

## Environment

- flashinfer-python main 5209e883 (built from source, `0.7.2+g5209e883`) with flashinfer-cubin from the same commit; also 0.7.2,
  0.7.1 and 0.6.18 (pip wheels). JIT only, no `flashinfer-jit-cache`.
- PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132, CUDA 13.x, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0.dev0, aarch64
- GPU: compute capability 10.7 (the issue does not depend on the GPU)
- Trigger in our case: `CUDA_HOME` pointed at a conda-style environment whose `include/` has no CUDA headers (they live under
  `targets/<arch>/include`). nvcc still finds its headers, so the CUDA sources of the GEMM module build fine; only the host
  C++ files of `trtllm_utils` (compiled with `-isystem $CUDA_HOME/include`) fail with `fatal error: cuda_fp16.h: No such file
  or directory`. That misconfiguration is ours; the point of this issue is how the autotuner reacts to it.

## Reproduction

`repro.py` (below) creates a copy of `$CUDA_HOME` without headers in `include/`, uses a fresh `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE`,
and tunes `mm_mxfp8(backend="cutlass")` (N = K = 4096) for M = 1, 16, 128 inside `with autotune(True)`. It counts the calls to
`delay_kernel` and their failures and the FlashInfer log records per level.

```
python repro.py            # broken CUDA_HOME
python repro.py --as-is    # unchanged CUDA_HOME, for comparison
```

Observed with main 5209e883 (broken CUDA_HOME):

```
"tune_seconds": 87.63,
"successful_configs": {},
"total_configs": {"mxfp8_gemm": 8},
"failed_tactics": {"mxfp8_gemm::CutlassMxfp8GemmRunner": 32},
"profiling_cache_entries": 0,
"delay_kernel_calls": 448,
"delay_kernel_failures": 448,
"delay_kernel_seconds": 37.3,
"first_error": "Ninja build failed. Ninja output:",
"flashinfer_log_records_by_level": {"INFO": 18}
```

i.e. 448 build attempts (14 profiles x 32 tactics), all failing, no WARNING, and the GEMM silently runs the fallback tactic
(results are finite). The same script on the same GPU type:

| flashinfer | CUDA_HOME | tune s | delay_kernel calls / failures | delay_kernel s | successful configs | records |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.6.18 | broken | 94.3 | 448 / 448 | 39.9 | 0 | INFO 16 |
| 0.7.1 | broken | 89.9 | 448 / 448 | 36.8 | 0 | INFO 18 |
| 0.7.2 | broken | 84.5 | 448 / 448 | 36.5 | 0 | INFO 18 |
| main 5209e883 | broken | 87.6 | 448 / 448 | 37.3 | 0 | INFO 18 |
| main 5209e883 | with headers | 53.4 | 256 / 0 | 3.6 | 8 | INFO 4 |

With a `CUDA_HOME` whose `include/` has the headers, `trtllm_utils` builds once and the same sweep succeeds (8 profiles
tuned, no failed tactic; most of the 53 s is the first build of the `mxfp8_gemm_cutlass` module). (The working row was measured
with `--as-is` and `CPATH=<toolkit>/targets/sbsa-linux/include`.) For this GEMM the fallback is ~3x slower than the tuned tactic
(about 100 us vs. <= 36 us per call at M <= 16, N = 25600, K = 6144, eager timing, 0.6.18), so a silent fallback can also cost
throughput.

Expected: one build attempt, then a clear WARNING (or an error) that profiling is unavailable, instead of N x 32 build attempts
and "unsupported tactic" at INFO level.

## Suggestions

1. Remember the failure of the `trtllm_utils` build (e.g. cache the exception, or build it once when entering
   `autotune(True)`), so a broken build costs one attempt instead of one per tactic.
2. Treat infrastructure errors (JIT build / import failures of the profiling helpers) differently from a tactic that fails on
   a given shape: log them once at WARNING with the first error line, and either abort the sweep for that op or fall back to
   timing without the delay kernel.
3. Optionally, include the number of failed vs. successful profiles in the "Autotuning process ends" message, so a sweep that
   produced nothing is visible at INFO level.

<details><summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
"""Repro: flashinfer.autotune retries a failed JIT build for every tactic and reports it only at debug level.

Usage (any GPU with the CUTLASS mm_mxfp8 backend, e.g. SM100/103/107/110):

    python repro.py                # breaks the JIT build on purpose: CUDA_HOME copy whose include/ has no CUDA headers
    python repro.py --as-is        # keep the current CUDA_HOME (shows the healthy behaviour on a normal toolkit)

The script runs in a fresh FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE, so nothing is reused from an existing JIT cache.  It tunes
mm_mxfp8(b

items.author: sylvesterkaczmarek

comments.author: codebreaker77
comments.body:
I'd like to help with a focused first slice of this RFC: a test-only scripted fault helper and an existing heartbeat regression migrated to use it.

Branch: https://github.com/codebreaker77/TensorRT-LLM/tree/test/18450-disagg-fault-harness

The helper targets a named async boundary, request/worker key and call occurrence. It provides explicit delay gates, dropped delivery, injected exceptions, a compact trace, and assertions for unused faults and still-active calls. It creates no background tasks and changes no production code or global clocks.

For a concrete existing consumer, test_heartbeat_survives_stalled_refresh_within_ttl now gates the first storage refresh instead of using a stall counter and long sleep. The worker's real per-attempt timeout cancels that call; retry succeeds. Original retry/deadline assertions remain, with an additional cancellation/retry trace and idle assertion.

Validation: 18 direct helper tests plus five watch-queue component checks and the migrated heartbeat regression pass on Windows Python 3.10 and Linux Python 3.12. The component checks execute unchanged production definitions and the actual regression function, while bypassing full package/native initialization. A temporary mutation removing the per-attempt timeout fails the regression as expected. Checked-in component tests retain normal production imports for supported CI; full-package collection has not been validated locally.

This initial slice does not provide virtual time, transport injection or full worker/transfer lifecycle coverage. The documented gate controls ordering only; the heartbeat test retains the real production timeout and clock.

Would this helper interface and first regression migration be a suitable initial contribution? Is the RFC author already working on the core fixture? I can adjust scope before requesting review.

items.title: [Performance]: copyBatchBlockOffsetsToDeviceKernel walks each long block-offset row with one CTA
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### Proposal to improve performance

`KVCacheManagerV2.copy_batch_block_offsets` launches `copyBatchBlockOffsetsToDeviceKernel` (`cpp/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerV2Utils.cu`) once per manager per step. Its grid is `(num_pools, num_seqs)`: a single 128-thread CTA walks each whole row of block offsets, two `cp.async` loads deep, reading the pinned host table. For long-context pools the rows are long; at 32772 blocks per sequence, each CTA runs 64 sequential load iterations. The kernel is then latency bound, with a handful of CTAs on the whole GPU.

Measured on Rubin, Kimi K3 decode (target manager with 2 pools, draft manager with 1, 32772 blocks per sequence, 1 sequence): 28-33 µs per call, about 60 µs per decode step on the critical path between steps.

Proposal: add a third grid dimension that splits each row into tiles of 1024 offsets, one CTA each, keeping the per-element arithmetic and the read-at-execution-time semantics unchanged. A Triton prototype of exactly this tiling (same reads, same integer arithmetic, bitwise-equal output) took the call from 27.7 µs to 4.0 µs (2 pools) and from 27.0 µs to 3.6 µs (1 pool) in a microbenchmark. End to end on Rubin, TP8 across 2 nodes (MNNVL), single request, it reduced decode step time by 0.014-0.043 ms depending on context length, and 128K TTFT by 0.043 s.

PR to follow (draft; the C++ version still needs a GPU build and microbenchmark).

items.title: [Bug]: MPIPoolExecutor is not defined with ENABLE_MULTI_DEVICE=OFF
items.author: xiaozhang8tuo
items.body_excerpt:
## Description

When TensorRT-LLM is built with `ENABLE_MULTI_DEVICE=OFF`, the default
single-GPU launch path fails with:

    NameError: name 'MPIPoolExecutor' is not defined

## Cause

In `tensorrt_llm/llmapi/mpi_session.py`, `MPIPoolExecutor` is imported only
inside `if ENABLE_MULTI_DEVICE:`, but
`GenerationExecutorProxy -> MpiPoolSession._start_mpi_pool` uses it on the
default startup path.

## Workaround

Set `TLLM_WORKER_USE_SINGLE_PROCESS=1`, which uses the single-process worker
path in `executor.py`.

## Environment

- TensorRT-LLM v1.3.0rc28
- Wheel built with
  `ENABLE_MULTI_DEVICE=OFF;BUILD_NCCL_EXTENSIONS=OFF;ENABLE_UCX=OFF;BUILD_DEEP_EP=OFF`
- CUDA 13.2, Python 3.10, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130
- Single H200, PyTorch backend

## Notes

Follow-up requested in #20580, which fixes `mpi_allgather` for the same build
configuration. This issue is not addressed by that PR.

items.title: [BUG] cutlass_library does not emit grouped NVFP4 (ue4m3) block-scaled GEMM for SM120, although example 79d runs that kernel
items.author: waynehacking8
items.body_excerpt:
## Description

`GenerateSM120_TensorOp_fp4_UMMA_gemm_with_block_scaled` (`python/cutlass_library/generator.py`, ~L11441) skips grouped **NVFP4 (ue4m3)** block-scaled GEMM tile descriptions for SM120, behind this comment:

```python
# grouped schedules only support ue8m0 (MXF4); NVF4 (ue4m3) grouped requires
# NVF4-specific PtrArray schedule tags not yet available
```

That comment appears to be **stale**:

- `to_grouped_schedule()` (`python/cutlass_library/library.py`, L1051-1052) already maps
  `Nvf4TmaWarpSpecialized{Cooperative,Pingpong}Sm120 → PtrArrayTmaWarpSpecialized{Cooperative,Pingpong}`.
- Example **`examples/79_blackwell_geforce_gemm/79d_blackwell_geforce_nvfp4_grouped_gemm.cu`** instantiates exactly this kernel — `ArchTag = cutlass::arch::Sm120`, `e2m1` operands, `ue4m3` SF, `KernelPtrArrayTmaWarpSpecialized{Cooperative,Pingpong}` — and runs correctly.

Because the grouped schedules collapse to `PtrArray*`, `is_nvf4(kernel_schedule)` is `False` in the grouped branch, so only the `ue8m0` (MXF4) grouped tiles are emitted and the NVFP4 grouped tiles are dropped.

### Effect

The library / profiler / autotuner can select grouped **MXFP4** on SM120 but not grouped **NVFP4**, so frameworks running NVFP4 MoE on consumer Blackwell (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 5090) don't get these grouped kernels and fall back to slower paths (related: #2800).

### Evidence (RTX PRO 6000, SM120, CUDA 13.0)

- Built + ran example 79d: both schedules `Disposition: Passed`, **303 / 253 TFLOPS**.
- Driving the grouped generator path directly (`GenerateSM120_TensorOp_fp4_UMMA_gemm_with_block_scaled(..., gemm_kind=GemmKind.GroupedBlockScaledUniversal3x)`):
  - today: 14 grouped fp4 ops, **0 NVFP4 (ue4m3) grouped**;
  - after adding an `is_grouped && ue4m3` clause: 28 ops, **14 NVFP4 grouped** (e.g. `cutlass3x_sm120_bstensorop_gemm_grouped_ue4m3xe2m1_ue4m3xe2m1_f32_void_f32_128x32x128_1x1x1_0_tnt_align32_warpspecialized_pingpong`).

### Proposed fix

In the grouped branch, key on the SF type instead of `is_nvf4(kernel_schedule)` (which only matches the non-grouped Sm120 tags):

```diff
         if (is_grouped_schedule and math_inst.element_scale_factor == DataType.ue8m0) or \
+           (is_grouped_schedule and math_inst.element_scale_factor == DataType.ue4m3) or \
            (not is_grouped_schedule and math_inst.element_scale_factor == DataType.ue4m3 and is_nvf4(kernel_schedule)) or \
            (not is_grouped_schedule and math_inst.element_scale_factor == DataType.ue8m0 and not is_nvf4(kernel_schedule)):
```

Happy to send this as a PR (with the stale comment corrected). I verified emission (0 → 14) and the kernel template via example 79d, but did not run a full `cutlass_profiler` build of all emitted tile variants locally — worth confirming in CI that every tile compiles (some SM120 tiles may hit Stages≥2 constraints; if so they can be pruned in the same clause).

cc @depaulmillz — this is the SM12x grouped / block-scaled generator area.

items.title: [DOC] TVM FFI guide examples fail due to missing imports, exception type and loader ABI
items.author: 0z5a
items.body_excerpt:
## Report incorrect documentation

**Location:** [TVM FFI compilation guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/blob/91843b71d90737e0a9b86f7d9df213cff5a3526f/media/docs/pythonDSL/guides/tvm_ffi_compilation.rst), at the v4.8.1 source revision.

**Problems:** Following the examples encounters several independent failures:

- The tuple example annotates its argument with `Tuple` without importing it.
- The keyword-argument example uses `cutlass.Float32` without importing `cutlass`.
- The intentionally invalid CUDA launch raises a DSL CUDA diagnostic that is not caught by the shown `except RuntimeError`.
- The keyword-argument export example omits `inspect` and `subprocess` imports. Its `load_module("./add_constant.so")` also selects the default CuTe ABI for a TVM FFI export; it needs `enable_tvm_ffi=True`.

**Verification:** Executed 12 extracted guide cases with CuTe DSL 4.8.1 in GH200 and H100 environments. Each case includes earlier guide definitions where needed and explicitly invokes functions defined by the guide. On both machines the original examples give 8 passes and 4 failures. With the imports, exception type and loader ABI corrected, all 12 pass, including numerical and expected-error checks. An additional GH200 check with imports repaired still fails at the export loader until the TVM FFI flag is supplied.

**Suggested fix:** Add the imports, catch `DSLCudaRuntimeError` in the invalid-launch example, and load the TVM FFI export with its matching ABI. This is a guide correction; no runtime change is needed.

items.title: [Bug] sm12x MoE CuTe-DSL kernels are never disk-cached — cute.compile hardcodes no_cache=True, so every fresh engine re-pays 15–40 s MLIR compiles per kernel shape
items.author: jhsmith409
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

The Blackwell sm12x fused-MoE path compiles all of its CuTe-DSL kernels through explicit
`cute.compile(...)`, which unconditionally disables the DSL's file cache. The only caching
layer is three in-process Python dicts, so **every engine start re-pays the full MLIR JIT
cost for every kernel specialization it touches** — measured at **~40 s** for the dynamic
kernel's first hit and **~15–18 s per small-`m` micro-kernel specialization**. In a serving
context (vLLM `--moe-backend=flashinfer_b12x`) these compiles land mid-request and freeze
the whole engine (vllm#47458: ~17.5 s stop-the-world stalls, all in-flight requests frozen
including mid-decode).

`CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR` / `CUTE_DSL_DISABLE_FILE_CACHING` have no effect on this path — the
gate that would consult them is short-circuited before they are read.

## Environment

- flashinfer 0.6.12, 0.6.13, and **0.6.15.post1** (all verified; `moe_dispatch.py` cache
  structure unchanged across them)
- nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.0 and **4.6.0** (both verified)
- SM120: RTX 5070 Ti (×2, TP/PP), RTX 5090 (unsharded), RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell — reproduced
  on all three in the vllm#47458 thread
- Model: `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` via vLLM `--moe-backend=flashinfer_b12x`

## Mechanism (exact code paths)

1. **The DSL hardcodes `no_cache=True` for explicit compiles.**
   `CompileCallable._compile` sets `kwargs["no_cache"] = True` unconditionally:
   - nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.0: `base_dsl/compiler.py:604-605`
   - nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.0: `base_dsl/compiler.py:1319`

2. **The file cache is gated behind `if not no_cache`** — both the load and the dump —
   so the env vars are never even consulted for explicit compiles:
   - 4.5.0: `base_dsl/dsl.py:1645` (load), `:1736` (dump)
   - 4.6.0: `base_dsl/dsl.py:2004` (load), `:2105` (dump); in-memory `jit_cache` lookups
     likewise skipped under `no_cache` at `:2012`, `:2293`

3. **The sm12x MoE dispatch only ever compiles through `cute.compile`,** with plain
   in-process dicts on top — nothing reaches disk:
   - 0.6.12/0.6.13: `blackwell_sm12x/moe_dispatch.py:676/912/1675` (compile sites);
     `_STATIC/_MICRO/_DYNAMIC_KERNEL_CACHE`
   - 0.6.15.post1: compile sites at `:697/:942/:1723`; caches at `:486/:733/:1524`

4. Compounding factor (tracked separately as #3836): the micro-kernel `cache_key`
   includes both `m` and `workspace.max_rows` (0.6.15.post1 `moe_dispatch.py:770-791`,
   fields at `:774`/`:778`), so workspace growth invalidates already-compiled small-batch
   entries even *within* a process lifetime. With no disk layer underneath, each
   invalidation is a full 15 s+ recompile, not a reload.

## Verification

Behavioral check from the vllm#47458 thread (credit @waynehacking8, on 0.6.12 / DSL 4.5.0):

- `cute.compile` of a trivial `@cute.jit` function leaves `CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR` **empty**.
- Calling the same jit function **directly** (implicit compile path) writes
  `cute_dsl_<hash>.mlir`, and a fresh process then logs `JIT cache hit IN-FILE`.
- Only the implicit direct-call path caches; flashinfer's MoE dispatch never uses it.

Source-level re-verification on 0.6.15.post1 / DSL 4.6.0 (2026-08-02, inside the
`vllm/vllm-openai` nightly image): every line cite in the Mechanism section above was
confirmed against the installed packages — the hardcoded `no_cache=True`, the
`if not no_cache` gates around both file-cache load and dump, the three `cute.compile`
sites, the three in-process dicts, and `m`/`max_rows` still present in the micro-kernel
cache key.

Measured first-hit compile costs (RTX PRO 6000, synthetic MoE E=32/topk=4 driving
`B12xMoEWrapper.run` exactly as vLLM's `FlashInferB12xExperts` does):

| kernel path | first hit | subsequent (same key) |
|---|---|---|
| dynamic (m-independent key) | ~40 s | 1–3 ms |
| micro m=1 | 14.9 s | ms |
| micro m=2 | 15.2 s | ms |
| micro m=64 | 18.3 s | ms |

Production symptom: vllm#47458 — py-spy captured 16 consecutive samples over 8.35 s pinned
in `b12x_fused_moe (flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/b12x_moe.py:166)` during a live
~17.5 s engine-wide stall; `perf` showed `_cutlass_ir.cpython-312.so` frames present only
during stalls.

## Why this deserves a disk layer even after #3836

#3836 stops *rekeying* (recompiles within one process). But serving engines restart —
deploys, config changes, crash recovery, autoscaling — and each fresh process re-pays the
entire compile set: ~40 s dynamic + 15–18 s per small-shape class. For a model like
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B this is 1–2 minutes of mid-serving stalls per engine lifetime that a
disk cache would reduce to milliseconds. The artifacts are deterministic products of
(kernel source, shape/config tuple, DSL version, arch) — exactly what file caches are for.

## Suggested fix directions

Either would resolve it; the first is contained entirely in flashinfer:

1. **flashinfer grows its own disk layer for sm12x MoE kernels**: serialize the compiled
   artifact keyed by the existing `cache_key` tuples + flashinfer version +
   nvidia-cutlass-dsl version + SM arch, under `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_DIR` (or a new env),
   loading into `_STATIC/_MICRO/_DYNAMIC_KERNEL_CACHE` on miss. The DSL's own
   `compile_and_cache` machinery demonstrates the artifact is serializable (the implicit
   path already writes/reads `.mlir` + compiled objects).
2. **Upstream: nvidia-cutlass-dsl honors its file cache under explicit `cute.compile`**
   (stop hardcoding `no_cache=True`, or add an opt-in kwarg flashinfer can pass).

A third, cheaper-but-partial option is an official warm-up API (the attempt in
vllm#47599 was closed unmerged): it moves the cost to boot but still re-pays it every
process start, and needs the largest-workspace-first ordering to avoid #3836 rekeying —
a disk cache composes with, rather than replaces, that.

## Cross-references

- vllm#47458 — serving-stall report this splits from (mechanism established in-thread by
  @waynehacking8; py-spy confirmation by me)
- flashinfer#3836 — the workspace-rekeying half (open)

items.title: [cuDNN][SDPA] SM 10.7 + cuDNN < 9.25: cuDNN is preferred but no forward plan builds; retrying the same shape segfaults (null MHAGraphCache entry)
items.author: lucifer1004
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Two related problems on a Vera Rubin GPU (compute capability 10.7) with torch 2.14.0+cu132 and its bundled cuDNN 9.24.0.

**1. Default SDPA dispatch fails instead of falling back.** `check_prefer_cudnn_attention()` returns true for all `major == 10` devices in CUDA >= 13 builds, so cuDNN is tried first. On SM 10.7, cuDNN 9.24's heuristics return only runtime-compiled engines (`eng10_k24=1_k27=0_k38=0_k40=3_k41=2` and three `eng8` configs). Each one fails in `cudnnBackendFinalize` with `CUDNN_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR_COMPILATION_FAILED: Encountered runtime kernel compilation failure at: compilationResult != NVRTC_SUCCESS`. The NVRTC version does not matter: 13.2 from the wheel and 13.4.92 give the same failure. Minimal repro:

```python
import torch, torch.nn.functional as F
q = torch.randn(1, 16, 1024, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, q, q)
# RuntimeError: cuDNN Frontend error: [cudnn_frontend] Error: No valid execution plans built.
```

Every shape that dispatches to cuDNN fails: seq len 256-8192, head_dim 32/64/128, bf16 and fp16, contiguous or strided. Flash, mem-efficient and math all work on the same inputs. cuDNN 9.25.1.1, 9.26.1.1 and 9.27.0.42 (loaded into the same process instead of 9.24) select `eng18`, which builds and runs correctly, and is about 3.4x faster than flash for `[1, 16, 8192, 64]`.

There is already an `is_unsupported_sm107` guard (`cudnn_version <= 92500`) in `check_cudnn_hardware_support`, but it only limits head_dim to 128. It does not stop cuDNN from being selected for the common head dims. Suggested fix: on SM 10.7 with cuDNN < 9.25, either reject cuDNN in `check_cudnn_hardware_support` / `check_prefer_cudnn_attention`, or extend the existing guard to all head dims.

**2. Calling again with the same shape after the failure segfaults.**

```python
import torch, torch.nn.functional as F
q = torch.randn(1, 16, 1024, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
for _ in range(2):
    try:
        F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, q, q)
    except RuntimeError as e:
        print(e)
# 1st call: RuntimeError (above); 2nd call: Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault
```

This also happens under `sdpa_kernel([SDPBackend.CUDNN_ATTENTION])`. The cause is in `aten/src/ATen/native/cudnn/MHA.cpp` (release/2.14 and main): `run_cudnn_SDP_fprop` does `getMHAGraphCache_().try_emplace(key, nullptr)` and then assigns `cache_it->second = build_graph(...)`. When `build_graph` throws, the `nullptr` entry stays in the cache. The next call with the same key takes the cache-hit path and dereferences `*cache_it->second`. The backward path (`run_cudnn_SDP_bprop`) uses the same `try_emplace(key, nullptr)` pattern. Fix: erase the entry when the build throws, or insert only after a successful build.

Problem 1 only affects builds that still ship cuDNN < 9.25 (e.g. the 2.14.x cu13 wheels with cuDNN 9.24). Problem 2 does not depend on the cuDNN version: any graph build failure poisons the cache for that shape, turning a recoverable exception into a crash. Downstream, this breaks applications that call SDPA on SM 10.7 (for example the DeepSeek-V4.1 vision encoder in TensorRT-LLM), and it means they cannot work around problem 1 with try/except.

Related (not duplicates): #190949 (d=256 cuDNN support surface on sm107, which added `is_unsupported_sm107`), #190388 (LRU bound for `MHAGraphCache`, does not touch the null-entry case), #193247 (CUDA 13.4 wheels moved to cuDNN 9.25).

### Versions

torch 2.14.0+cu132 (git 08187d9e0f), cuDNN 9.24.0 (runtime and compile time), cudnn-frontend 1.26 (bundled), CUDA 13.2 wheel runtime, also reproduced with NVRTC 13.4.92. GPU: Vera Rubin, compute capability 10.7. aarch64.

items.title: varlen_attn: no CPU fallback, and the error does not say CUDA is required
items.author: konard
items.body_excerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

`torch.nn.attention.varlen.varlen_attn` only runs on CUDA (and ROCm). On CPU it fails inside the dispatcher with an error that does not mention `varlen_attn`, and its docstring does not say which devices are supported. So every library that switches from `flash_attn.flash_attn_varlen_func` to `varlen_attn` has to write its own per-sequence fallback to run, or test, the same model on CPU.

I hit this while replacing the `flash-attn` wheel with `varlen_attn` in a downstream project. flash-attn publishes no wheel for torch ≥ 2.9, so the wheel was what held the project on torch 2.8. Our CI has no GPU, so upstream's model is tested on CPU, and the attention call needs a CPU path.

**Reproduction** (torch 2.14.1+cpu, Python 3.14, Linux x86_64; the same happens with the CUDA wheel on a CPU tensor):

```python
import torch
from torch.nn.attention.varlen import varlen_attn

cu = torch.tensor([0, 3, 8], dtype=torch.int32)
q = torch.randn(8, 2, 16, dtype=torch.bfloat16)  # (total_tokens, heads, head_dim)
varlen_attn(q, q, q, cu, cu, 5, 5, window_size=(-1, 0))
```

```
NotImplementedError: Could not run 'aten::_flash_attention_forward' with arguments from the 'CPU' backend. ...
```

**Affected versions:** 2.10.0 through 2.14.1. All of them dispatch straight to `_flash_attention_forward`, or to cuDNN on CUDA (`torch/nn/attention/varlen.py`).

**Workaround downstream:** run one `scaled_dot_product_attention` per packed sequence, with a bottom-right causal mask when `q_len < k_len` (flash-attn's convention):

```python
outs = []
for i in range(len(cu_q) - 1):
    q_i = q[cu_q[i]:cu_q[i + 1]].transpose(0, 1)          # (heads, Lq, d)
    k_i = k[cu_k[i]:cu_k[i + 1]].transpose(0, 1)
    v_i = v[cu_k[i]:cu_k[i + 1]].transpose(0, 1)
    mask = None
    if causal:
        lq, lk = q_i.shape[1], k_i.shape[1]
        mask = torch.ones(lq, lk, dtype=torch.bool, device=q.device).tril(lk - lq)
    outs.append(F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q_i, k_i, v_i, attn_mask=mask, scale=scale,
                                               enable_gqa=k_i.shape[0] != q_i.shape[0]).transpose(0, 1))
out = torch.cat(outs)
```

(The full version, with tests against a reference implementation, is `flash_attn_varlen_func` in https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/blob/issue-21-f7500eb08675/scripts/unimedvl_server.py.)

**Suggested fix**, either or both of:

1. **A math fallback in `varlen_attn`** for devices without a flash kernel (CPU, MPS, XPU). It would be the loop above, or one SDPA call with a block-diagonal mask built from `cu_seq_q`/`cu_seq_k`, with `window_size` mapped onto the mask. It would be slow, but it would give the same numbers, which is what CPU tests and CPU inference of small models need. The guard could look like `if not query.is_cuda: return _varlen_attn_math(...)`, placed before the `torch.ops.aten._flash_attention_forward` call.
2. **If CPU is out of scope**, the docstring could say "CUDA (sm80+) and ROCm only", and `varlen_attn` could raise a `NotImplementedError` naming itself and the device, instead of the dispatcher's message about `aten::_flash_attention_forward`.

I searched open and closed issues for `varlen_attn cpu` and found nothing. #171814 (the RFC) and #179382 (dropout) do not mention CPU.

### Alternatives

Keep the per-sequence SDPA loop in every downstream project, as above.

### Additional context

Related: #171814, #174961.
